html:
The system set up by the emperor Diocletian to rule the Roman Empire with four men instead of one. It ran from 293 to 324.

Two senior emperors, the augusti, shared the empire: Diocletian in the east and Maximian in the west. Each had a junior partner and chosen heir, a caesar: Galerius and Constantius. Each of the four had his own army and court close to a frontier. Rome itself lost its role as a seat of power to cities such as Milan, Trier, Sirmium and Nicomedia.

The plan worked as defence but failed as a way to pass on power. When Diocletian and Maximian stepped down in 305, the sons left out of the scheme, Constantine and Maxentius, claimed thrones of their own. Years of civil war followed until Constantine ruled alone in 324. A famous porphyry statue of the four tetrarchs embracing, now in Venice, shows the ideal of unity.
sum: The system set up by the emperor Diocletian to rule the Roman Empire with four men instead of one. It ran from 293 to 324.
